summary: Repaired and secured the node1 status service. It persists across reboot on RHEL 7.9, returns the preserved status document only for STATUS\n, rejects other requests, and restricts access to statusd and status-readers.
actions_performed: Provisioned statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers.
Repaired server.py with exact request validation.
Set the socket to statusd:status-readers mode 0660 and protected the document.
Restarted node1 safely and verified full recovery.

evidence.summary: Pre-change and post-restart SHA-256 values match: 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b.
status-reader belongs to status-readers; outsider does not; identities persisted after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Restrict service access to statusd and status-readers
evidence.summary: Socket is statusd:status-readers mode 0660. Both authorized identities connect successfully; outsider receives permission denied and cannot read the document.

evidence.requirement: Return the document for STATUS newline and an error otherwise
evidence.summary: Authorized response hashes and byte-for-byte comparisons match the document; invalid requests return ERROR.

evidence.requirement: Operate persistently without changing the legacy OS or kernel
evidence.summary: statusd.service is enabled and active after reboot; RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 remain installed.

Captured healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgment, proved boot ID changed from b35fad86-4e61-46bf-bbd2-0dadcedb685d to 3d0afbf4-7f98-42c2-8c82-a61aea582ecd, then verified service, socket, data, roles, protocol, and access denial recovered.
